title: Try: ask a question
text: Demo Try: ask a question Pick a graph and a question; Hermes runs in your browser and shows every stage. The sample questions replay recorded replies of Llama 3.1 8B; for your own questions, use a model you run or paste its replies. What runs where Hermes's own Python package runs in your browser under Pyodide , the same wheel the benchmarks run, and its queries run on Oxigraph compiled to WebAssembly, the engine Hermes uses for local graphs. No server of ours is involved. Only the model is not here: Ollama on your computer is detected under My model , a small model can run in the page on WebGPU, or you can paste replies. Your files stay in the page. Loading… Reading it Ontology slice : what the model is shown of the ontology. Classes and properties are chosen by the question's words, then completed with what the chosen classes use; values and entities are those the question names. Repair : each change, with its reason. Problems that remain are sent back to the model while the budget allows. Plan : the query as relational algebra, as written and as rewritten, with the estimated rows of every operator. Price and spend : what the run was expected to cost before each step, and what it cost. A step that would go over the budget is not taken. Previous Overview Next Try: plan a query

title: Evaluation
text: hermes.experiments Evaluation Six benchmarks in one format, a scorer that reproduces every published Text2SPARQL 2026 score, and runs that record their config, commit, answers and cost. On this page Benchmarks Runs Results Benchmarks Text2SPARQL 2026 corporate (CK26) and DBpedia (DB26), their 2025 editions, QALD-9-plus and QALD-10, fetched with hermes data fetch . CK26 is CK25 paraphrased, so CK25 is not a development set for CK26. Runs hermes run configs/ck26/hermes.yaml hermes sweep configs/sweeps/hermes.yaml # Hermes, its ablations, and baselines hermes report Each run writes its config, commit, every prediction with its cost, and metrics under results/ . Scores: the official set F1 and F1-nDCG, a strict variant, and the subset whose gold answers reproduce on the local engine. Results The pipeline's runs are in results/ . Previous Graphs Next Baselines

title: Graphs
text: hermes.graph Graphs A KnowledgeGraph is a store to query, a schema to read the ontology from, and preferred prefixes. Stores answer SPARQL 1.1 JSON, so files and endpoints are interchangeable. from hermes import KnowledgeGraph kg = KnowledgeGraph.from_files("ontology.ttl", "data.ttl", schema=["ontology.ttl"]) kg = KnowledgeGraph.from_endpoint("https://dbpedia.org/sparql") from hermes import benchmarks; kg = benchmarks.graph("corporate") # data/graphs.yaml Oxigraph (default for files), rdflib , endpoint and browser (the page's Oxigraph under Pyodide) stores; a caching decorator memoizes results and counts executions. Source: stores.py . Statistics are read once for local graphs and one predicate at a time from endpoints ( statistics.py ). Entity linking matches labels exactly, or by their words ( linking.py ). Previous Pricing and budgets Next Evaluation

title: Hermes
text: Ontology-based natural-language querying over knowledge graphs Hermes Ask a question in English; Hermes writes SPARQL from the slice of the ontology the question needs, repairs it, plans it as relational algebra with the graph's statistics, and runs it, pricing every model call and graph query before it spends it. On this page How it works Quick start What is measured Ask a question Plan a query GitHub How it works The ontology is the schema and the knowledge graph is the data. A question goes through seven stages: Refine the ontology slice the question needs Examples synthetic pairs from the graph Generate one model call writes SPARQL Repair prefixes, terms, types, probes Plan relational algebra, rewritten Price checked against the budget Execute the plan runs on the graph One model call writes the query; everything after it is checked before it costs anything, and the model is asked again only when a check fails and the budget allows. See Pipeline . Quick start git clone https://github.com/lamng3/hermes.git && cd hermes pip install -e ".[dev]" hermes data fetch ck26 # the Text2SPARQL corporate graph and benchmark hermes ask --graph corporate "Which department does Ms. Brant belong to?" from hermes import Budget, Hermes, KnowledgeGraph kg = KnowledgeGraph.from_files("ontology.ttl", "data.ttl", schema=["ontology.ttl"]) answer = Hermes(kg, budget=Budget(llm_calls=3)).ask("Which cities hosted the Winter Olympics?") print(answer.sparql, answer.rows, answer.spend.total) The model is a local one through Ollama by default, or any OpenAI-compatible API; see Python and CLI . What is measured On the gold queries of the Text2SPARQL 2026 benchmarks, every plan that ran returned the engine's answers, and the optimizer cut the work; Planner has the details. The pipeline's accuracy and cost are on Evaluation . CK26 (local) DB26 (DBpedia endpoint) gold queries whose plans ran and gave the engine's answers 48 of 48 41 of 41 intermediate rows, as written → optimized 1,302,989 → 106,719 1,097,107 → 1,060,291 plan seconds, as written → optimized 4.67 → 1.35 68.4 → 29.7 Next Try: ask a question

title: Pipeline
text: hermes.pipeline Pipeline A question goes through seven stages; each reports to observers as it starts and ends, and each prices what it is about to spend. On this page The ontology catalog The ontology refiner Few-shot examples Generate The query refiner Observers Refine the ontology slice the question needs Examples synthetic pairs from the graph Generate one model call writes SPARQL Repair prefixes, terms, types, probes Plan relational algebra, rewritten Price checked against the budget Execute the plan runs on the graph The ontology catalog Everything the model may need to know about the graph. From the ontology: classes and properties with labels, comments, declared domains and ranges. From the data: how often each term is used, which properties the instances of each class use, which classes a property's objects belong to, whether a property holds literals or entities, the values of properties with few distinct values (currencies, countries), and the members of classes with at most 100 instances (departments, product categories). Built once per graph; 0.1 s for the corporate graph. Source: catalog.py . The ontology refiner Hermes keeps the classes, properties and values that rank highest for the question, adds the properties the chosen classes' instances use and the classes at both ends of the chosen properties, and links the entities the question names: exact labels, members of small classes the question names, and capitalized mentions ("Ms. Brant" finds "Karen Brant"). Ranking is pluggable: BM25 by default, or embeddings from any OpenAI-compatible or Ollama endpoint ( retrieval.py ). Properties (subject → object): - pv:memberOf "member of": Agent, Employee, Manager → Department Values that occur in the graph: - pv:addressCountry "France" Entities named in the question: - prodi:prod-cat-Compensator "Compensator" (Product Category) Few-shot examples Built from the graph, never from benchmark questions ( synthetic.py ): template queries over the catalog (an entity's attribute, a relation either way, instances with a listed value, a count, a superlative, two hops), filled with sampled entities and kept when they return 1 to 50 rows. The model writes the question each query answers from its terms' labels, and the pair is kept only if the pipeline, without examples, answers that question with the same answers (F1 ≥ 0.7). hermes fewshot build --graph corporate writes data/fewshot/corporate.jsonl ; the two closest examples go in each prompt. Generate One call. The prompt is built by a builder ( prompt.py ) from instructions, prefixes, the ontology slice, the examples and the question. The query refiner Cheapest first, each change recorded ( repair.py ): declare prefixes the query uses but forgot; move ORDER BY and LIMIT out of WHERE; replace an unknown property or class by the closest known name; replace an entity IRI the graph does not mention by the entity whose label matches it; check types: a class used as a property, a literal where a property holds entities, an entity where it holds literals; probe: one ASK query per pattern about a named entity, so empl-Heinrich.Hoch a pv:Manager is caught before the query runs empty; send what is still wrong back to the model, at most twice, while the budget allows. An answer with no rows is sent back once more. Observers from hermes.pipeline.events import Recorder, Printer answer = Hermes(kg, observers=[Printer()]).ask(question) # one line per stage Previous Try: plan a query Next Planner

title: Try: plan a query
text: Demo Try: plan a query No model needed. Paste a SPARQL query or pick a sample; Hermes translates it into relational algebra, rewrites it with the graph's statistics, runs both plans, and checks their answers against the engine. Loading… Reading it Each line of a plan is one operator: scan a triple pattern, ⋈ a join, σ a filter, π a projection, ⟕ OPTIONAL, γ grouping. est is the planner's estimate of the rows, got what the run produced. The plan executor treats the graph as a black box that answers single-pattern queries, so the join order decides how much is fetched; see Planner . Previous Try: ask a question Next Pipeline

title: Planner
text: hermes.planner Planner A query becomes a relational-algebra plan, the optimizer rewrites it with the graph's statistics, and the plan executor runs it against a graph that answers only single-pattern queries. On this page Relational algebra Estimates Rewrite rules Executors Study on gold queries Relational algebra A triple pattern is a relation over its variables, a basic graph pattern the natural join of its patterns, and every other SPARQL operator a relational one: σ FILTER, π SELECT, ⟕ OPTIONAL, ∪ UNION, − MINUS, ε BIND, δ DISTINCT, τ ORDER BY, λ LIMIT and OFFSET, γ GROUP BY. translate keeps the patterns in the written order, so every reordering is the optimizer's and can be measured. Source: algebra.py . hermes plan --graph corporate --query 'SELECT ?name ?email WHERE { ?p pv:email ?email . ?p pv:name ?name . ?p pv:memberOf ?d . ?d pv:name "Marketing" . FILTER(CONTAINS(?name, "S")) }' Optimized π ?name ?email est 10.2 · got 2 └─ ⋈ ├─ ⋈ │ ├─ ⋈ │ │ ├─ scan (?d pv:name "Marketing") est 1.2 · got 1 │ │ └─ scan (?p pv:memberOf ?d) est 53.0 · got 10 │ └─ σ CONTAINS(?name, "S") │ └─ scan (?p pv:name ?name) got 10 └─ scan (?p pv:email ?email) est 53.0 · got 2 as written optimized rows fetched 160 23 intermediate rows 280 41 Estimates System R (Selinger et al., SIGMOD 1979), from the graph's statistics: per predicate its triples, distinct subjects and objects; per class its instances; property paths from their predicates. A scan joined after operands that bind its variables is priced as an index access, about (distinct bindings) × (rows per binding), because that is how the executor runs it. The cost of a plan is C_out, the summed sizes of its scans and joins. Source: estimate.py . Rewrite rules Each rule is a command that rewrites the plan and logs what it did ( rules.py ); the optimizer applies them in order, and a list of rules can be passed instead. push selections : each σ moves to the lowest operator that binds all of its variables in every solution. order joins : each join group is reordered by dynamic programming over left-deep orders without cartesian products, minimizing C_out; each selection goes right after the operand that binds its last variable. prune scans : a scan fetches only the variables used above it. Executors The plan executor runs scans as single-pattern queries and joins as hash joins, or bind joins that send the left side's bindings with the scan (up to 500, 100 per query); every other operator is evaluated by rdflib's SPARQL engine over its children's rows, with EXISTS and property paths reading the graph through the same single-pattern queries. The engine executor sends the query text to the store and is the reference. Source: executor.py . Study on gold queries experiments/planner_study.py plans every distinct gold query of a benchmark as written and optimized, runs both, and compares their answers with the engine's. Report: results/planner . CK26 DB26 same answers as the engine 46 41 same up to rows tied under ORDER BY with LIMIT 1 0 the engine is wrong, the plan right (Oxigraph 0.5.11 reads a / b * c as a / (b * c) ) 1 0 the engine cannot run the gold query 2 0 a scan over 200,000 rows, or the endpoint failed 0 9 plans that ran and gave other answers 0 0 intermediate rows, as written → optimized 1,302,989 → 106,719 1,097,107 → 1,060,291 rows fetched, as written → optimized 56,460 → 48,429 622,861 → 588,535 plan seconds, as written → optimized 4.67 → 1.35 68.4 → 29.7 q-error of the row estimate, median / 90th percentile 1.10 / 5.17 1.41 / 10.79 Most gold queries have one or two patterns and nothing to reorder; the savings come from the others, such as CK26 question 28 (intermediate rows 419,035 → 3,353) and DB26 question 41 (rows fetched 32,896 → 27). title: Pricing and budgets
text: hermes.pricing Pricing and budgets Every model call and every plan is priced before it runs; a budget caps calls, tokens, dollars, graph queries and rows, and a run reports what each stage was expected to cost and what it cost. On this page Prices Budgets Pricing graph queries Prices A Price counts model calls, input and output tokens, dollars when the model has a list price, graph queries and rows fetched. A model call is priced from its prompt (four characters a token) with 400 output tokens; a plan from the planner's estimates of the queries and rows its executor will fetch. Source: budget.py , list prices in prices.py . Budgets from hermes import Budget, Hermes answer = Hermes(kg, budget=Budget(llm_calls=3, tokens=20_000, rows=50_000)).ask(question) answer.spend.to_dict() # per stage: estimated and actual answer.error # "over budget at execute: rows would reach 61,204, over the cap of 50,000" A step that would break the budget is not taken: a repair the budget cannot afford is skipped and the problems are reported; a plan over the row cap is not run. BudgetedLLM decorates any model client with the same check. Pricing graph queries The graph side of a price comes from the planner (see estimates ): a plan's rows fetched are estimated scan by scan, with bind joins priced as index accesses, before anything is sent. On the corporate graph the median q-error of the result's row estimate is 1.10; on DBpedia, where statistics come from the endpoint one predicate at a time, 1.41. Previous Planner Next Graphs

title: Python and CLI
text: Reference Python and CLI Ask, plan, build few-shot examples, run benchmarks, and serve the Text2SPARQL challenge API. On this page Command line Python Models Command line hermes ask --graph corporate "Who is Heinrich Hoch's manager?" --calls 3 --rows 50000 hermes ask --files data.ttl --ontology onto.ttl "..." hermes plan --graph corporate --file query.rq hermes fewshot build --graph corporate --count 30 hermes data fetch ck26 db26 hermes run configs/ck26/hermes.yaml hermes sweep configs/sweeps/hermes.yaml hermes report hermes serve --config configs/ck26/hermes.yaml # the Text2SPARQL challenge API Python from hermes import Budget, Hermes, KnowledgeGraph from hermes import planner answer = Hermes(kg, budget=Budget(llm_calls=3)).ask(question) optimized = planner.plan(sparql, kg) result = planner.PlanExecutor(kg)(optimized.query) Models Ollama by default ( HERMES_OLLAMA_MODEL ), or HERMES_LLM_PROVIDER = openai , anthropic , together , huggingface , vllm or modal with the provider's key. Completions can be cached on disk so runs replay ( llm.py ). Previous Baselines
